**Chinese name:** 飞腾信息技术有限公司 (Fēiténg Xìnxī Jìshù Yǒuxiàn Gōngsī)

::: {.callout-tip}
## Why This Matters
Jointly established in 2014 by China Electronics Corporation (a central state-owned enterprise), the Tianjin Binhai New Area government, and the Tianjin Advanced Technology Research Institute — one of the most directly state-backed design houses in this tracker. Added to the Entity List in April 2021 over supercomputing ties to Chinese military modernization; TSMC subsequently stopped supplying it. Remains privately held (not publicly listed), so financial disclosure is limited, but reported a notable deployment milestone in February 2026: its chips went into production for the first time at a major international hub airport (Ürümqi Tianshan International, 10M+ annual passenger throughput) in civil aviation systems.
:::

## What does this firm design?

ARM-based CPUs across server, desktop, and embedded product lines, used primarily in government and state-sector systems. Verified 2026 milestones: the Tengyun S5000C-E paired with China Telecom Cloud scored #1 worldwide on SPEC Cloud IaaS 2018 (168.2, May 2026); both S5000C and S5000C-E entered China Mobile's 2026–2027 PC/server procurement (late September 2026); the desktop D3000 took a 130,000-unit win at a major state-owned bank and the D3000M won 100% of a provincial government unified tender (~60,000 units, September 2026). At its August 2026 12th-anniversary briefing Phytium disclosed its first AI accelerator, the 飞腾A1000, now in mass production, a 'CPU+XPU dual-drive' roadmap, and cumulative R&D spend over ¥6 billion; a June 2026 CCB-Tianjin retrospective said an IPO is imminent ('上市在即') — no CSRC/exchange filing visible as of October 2026.
